review_type: Fresh-context AI review; not a human expert review and not independent training. Reviewer initially read only the three named masked input files. No author keys, generators, protocols, previous packets, or author judgments were accessed.

assessment.correctness_ambiguity: All numerical alternatives explicitly checked. Each item has exactly one correct option. Wording disambiguates subset labeling, selection order, graph direction, replacement and rounding. No correctness or ambiguity blocker found.
assessment.rounding: All nine urn posteriors computed as exact fractions; half-up nearest whole percentage point independently checked by exact interval membership. Adjacent percentage alternatives remain uniquely resolvable.
assessment.difficulty_status: No response data were inspected. Difficulty labels are qualitative forecasts, not empirical calibration. Actual model error rates and benefit from added computation remain unknown.
assessment.option_cues: Both options have matched formatting and no answer-explanation leakage. Small two-option sets permit 50% chance performance. Incorrect alternatives are numerically nearby; no universal higher/lower shortcut or positional shortcut is supported. Position counts are balanced within each split and near-balanced by family. The calibration and reserved urn blocks both follow A-B-A-B, a visible local pattern when solutions are exposed; this is not a logically valid stem-only answer cue and does not block the narrow numerical calibration, but item order should not be treated as an independent difficulty signal.
assessment.computation_scope: Narrow arithmetic templates: recurrences require 6-9 dependent modular steps; subsets require at most 20 triples; shortest paths are very small positive-weight DAGs, frequently solved by a direct edge or visible two-edge route; urns use two likelihoods and a Bayes update. These are valid manageable resource/calibration tasks but do not alone establish broad difficult-reasoning ability.
assessment.template_overlap: All three splits reuse the same four exact verbal templates with parameter changes. This is intended-looking within-family transfer and a material limitation on claims of novel-template generalization. No exact duplicate full stem was found. Repeated urn evidence structure, fixed six-object subsets, six-vertex DAGs, and fixed-order recurrences make solution strategies reusable.
assessment.recommended_disposition: Proceed with resource tests and calibration if claims remain limited to these four computational templates. No must-fix item blocker. Consider separate novel-template evaluation if broader generalization is the target.
